authorship: Assistant-authored manual synthesis from direct GitHub review; terminal does not infer or select strategies.
principles: Use point-in-time causal eligibility; never revive fixed-universe survivorship bias.
Treat old REJECT decisions as whole-system verdicts, not proof that every signal primitive inside was useless.
Prefer sparse trend/momentum setups with asymmetric payoff over high-turnover rotation.
Use OHLCV primitives as confluence around a setup, not standalone alpha claims.
Protect downside with immutable initial stop and hard portfolio governor, but do not cap winners with a fixed profit target.
Allow a proven winner to mature into a long runner when trend structure remains valid.
Use reversal only as a small independent sleeve; it is not the primary engine.
Cost robustness is measured at 1x and 2x; no result is promoted automatically from the same research period.

evidence.lesson: Breakout can create large winners, but the old whole-system drawdown was unacceptable. Carry forward the setup, not the old risk envelope.
Momentum/reacceleration had substantial gross economic value but excessive drawdown. Preserve alpha logic and redesign risk.
Heavy throttling reduced drawdown but also suppressed too much return. Test soft throttle separately rather than making it mandatory.
Reversal is not strong enough as the core engine, but is useful as a smaller independent route in non-trending states.
Frequent rotation created churn. Do not replace a valid incumbent merely because a new candidate appears.
Use regime + trend + relative strength + setup + volume/structure/liquidity confluence with causal next-open execution. Fibonacci is a soft score only.
Pullback/reacceleration are setup types inside a trend engine, not a standalone universal strategy.
Protect proven winners from severe giveback, but distinguish them from stale losers; one fixed holding horizon is wrong.
Fixed-universe backtests can be badly misleading. New strategy must use the canonical point-in-time candidate/eligibility surface.
Do not treat individual indicators as alpha. Use them only as confluence around a historically supported setup.
Core should be sparse, cost-aware, trend-aligned, cross-sectionally ranked, with confirmed pullback or contraction breakout and convex trailing exits.
Do not return to broad slot bypass, pyramiding, reacquisition, or heuristic replacement as the main engine. First prove the trade recipe itself.
